commitResults.messageTitle: Add use cases for ClientBookThree to the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG still has AB3's single use case for deleting a person, which
does not describe how a freelance developer uses ClientBookThree.

Let's replace it with ten use cases covering adding, listing, finding,
editing and deleting contacts, tagging contacts with projects, viewing
a project's contacts, updating a client's engagement status, and
undoing changes. Each has a main success scenario and extensions for
invalid input, duplicates and empty results.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept apostrophes, hyphens and accents in names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names may only contain letters, digits and spaces, so real names such
as O'Brien, Jean-Luc, Raj s/o Kumar, or names with accented letters,
are rejected. Rejecting valid real-world input is a feature flaw, as
the user has no way to record the contact under their actual name.

Let's allow letters from any language, digits, spaces, and the
characters ' - . , / in names. A name must still start with a letter
or digit, so blank names stay invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept phone numbers with +, spaces and brackets
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone numbers may only contain digits, so numbers written the usual
way, such as +65 9123 4567, (65) 9123-4567 or 1234 5678 (HP), are
rejected. Freelancers often have overseas clients, so country codes
and separators are common, and the user should not have to strip them.

Let's allow digits, spaces, letters for labels such as HP or ext, and
the characters + - ( ) . / in phone numbers. A number must still start
with a digit, + or ( and contain at least 3 digits.

Test values that relied on the old rule are changed to values that
remain invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the address optional when adding a contact
commitResults.messageBody:
add requires a/ADDRESS, but a freelancer often does not know a
contact's address, e.g. a remote client or a client's finance officer.
The user then has to make one up, which puts wrong data in the client
book.

Let's make a/ADDRESS optional. A contact added without one gets
Address.EMPTY rather than null, so other code needs no null checks.
It is saved as an empty string, and a missing address field in the
data file is read the same way. The contact card leaves the address
line out, and the success message does not show an empty address.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a command to delete a project
commitResults.messageBody:
Projects can be created, and clients added to and removed from them,
but a project can never be deleted, so finished or mistaken projects
stay in the client book.

Let's add "project delete PROJECT", which deletes the project and
removes it from every client in it. The clients and their other
projects are kept, and the reply says how many clients the project
was removed from. The name is matched ignoring case and extra spaces,
as in the other project commands.

The parser test that used "delete Portal" as an unknown subcommand
now uses "deletePortal" instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show each client's projects on their contact card
commitResults.messageBody:
A client's projects can only be seen with "project list INDEX", one
client at a time, so the main list does not show who is on which
project.

Let's add a line below the email on each card, e.g. "Projects: Client
Portal, Website Redesign", in the order the client joined them. A
client on no project gets no such line. Joining or leaving a project
changes no client, so the list redraws its cards whenever the
client-project memberships change. Logic now exposes the client book
for this.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Java skips assert statements unless assertions are enabled, so the
checks in our code never run when the app is started with
./gradlew run. Gradle already enables them for tests.

Let's enable assertions for the run task too.

A freelancer has no way to record where each engagement stands, so
they cannot see which clients need attention.

Let's add a status to each contact: lead, active, on hold or done, or
none for contacts such as a client's finance officer.

- "status INDEX STATUS" sets it, and "status INDEX none" clears it.
- "list s/STATUS" lists only the contacts with that status.
- The status is shown on the contact card and saved to the data file.
  A file without statuses still loads, with every status set to none.

Status names ignore case, and hyphens, underscores or extra spaces
count as one space, so "On-Hold" works. edit keeps the status.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep a short note against a contact
commitResults.messageBody:
A freelancer has nowhere to record context about a contact, such as
their timezone or how they prefer to be contacted.

Let's add a note to each contact.

- "note INDEX TEXT" adds or replaces it, and "note INDEX" removes it.
- Everything after the index is the note, so it may contain any
  characters, including prefixes such as t/.
- The note is shown on the contact card and saved to the data file.
  A file without notes still loads, with every note empty.

edit keeps the note.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover ListCommand#equals for the same object
commitResults.messageBody:
Codecov reports the same-object shortcut in ListCommand#equals as
untested.

Let's check that a ListCommand equals itself.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an optional company to contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
Clients are usually reached through the company they work for, but a
contact had nowhere to record it, so users put it in tags or the name.

Let's add an optional company field, set with c/COMPANY in add and
edit, and removed with an empty c/ in edit. It is shown under the
contact's name and saved with the contact; data files without it still
load. The sample data now includes companies.

Master now has client statuses (#60), which also added a field to
Person, so both changes touched the same constructor, storage and card
code.

Let's keep both: a contact has a status and a note. Person gets one
constructor taking both (the short one still means neither), edit keeps
both, both are saved, and the card shows both lines.

Master now has client statuses (#60), which also added a field to
Person, so both changes touched the same constructor, storage and edit
code.

Let's keep both: a contact has a company and a status. Person gets one
constructor taking both (the short one still means neither), edit
changes the company but keeps the status, and both are saved. Contacts
built with a company, by add or in the sample data, start without a
status.

Master now has contact notes (#61) as well as statuses, and notes also
added a field to Person, so both changes touched the same constructor,
storage and edit code again.

Let's keep all three: a contact has a company, a status and a note.
Person's full constructor takes all three (the short one still means
none), edit changes the company but keeps the status and note, and all
three are saved.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let a contact be created without an address
commitResults.messageBody:
The address is optional, but Person had no constructor for a contact
without one, so callers had to pass Address.EMPTY themselves, unlike
the company, status and note, which the short constructor fills in.

Let's add a constructor without the address that uses Address.EMPTY,
as suggested in review.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find contacts by company as well as by name
commitResults.messageBody:
Users often remember the company a client works for better than the
client's name, but find only looked at names.

Let's make find match a keyword against the name or the company, with
the same partial, case-insensitive matching as names. A contact without
a company matches on the name only.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the Model class diagram for ClientBook, projects and new fields
commitResults.messageBody:
The Model class diagram still showed AB3's AddressBook, and none of the
fields or classes added since: projects, and each contact's company,
status and note.

Let's redraw it to match the code: ClientBook with its person, project
and client-project lists, and Person with Company, Status and Note. The
DG text now describes these too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the Model class diagram at its natural size
commitResults.messageBody:
The redrawn diagram is wider, so at the old width of 450 its text was
smaller than the surrounding DG text.

Let's show it at its natural width of 650.

Master now has the final version of partial-name find (#64), which
dropped "find reset view", so this branch no longer needs to keep it.

Also, as suggested in review, let's remove NameContainsKeywordsPredicate:
find now uses NameOrCompanyContainsKeywordsPredicate, and the tests that
used the old predicate use the new one. Its edge cases (middle of a
word, accented letters, keywords that look like regular expressions,
keywords longer than the name) are kept in the new predicate's tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show ClientProject as an association class in the Model diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
ClientProject was drawn as an ordinary class pointing to Person and
Project, which hides that it describes the many-to-many link between
them.

Let's draw it as an association class on the Person-Project
association, as suggested in review, and say so in the DG text.
